spec.purpose: Shape verification (pipeline Phase 5, after type-inference + method-call-resolver + shape-tracker). It builds a class/interface → member-name index (HAS_METHOD for classes, EXTENDS-chain closed with cycle protection; HAS_METHOD + HAS_PROPERTY for interfaces), then for every dotted CALL that does NOT already carry a CALLS/CALLS_REMOTE edge it traces the receiver (CALL -READS_FROM-> V, or CALL -DERIVES_FROM-> PROPERTY_ACCESS -READS_FROM-> V, with one REFERENCE -READS_FROM-> deref hop) to a declaration with an INSTANCE_OF edge, and if the called method name (suffix after the last '.') is absent from that type's member set it creates an ISSUE node (id `issue::shape-violation::<callId>`, name "Method .X not found on Y", metadata JSON: severity=warning, category=shape-violation, method, receiverType, callName, line). It currently does this via N+1 IPC round-trips (getOutgoingEdges + getNode per CALL and per HAS_METHOD edge) and times out at 60s.

writes: plugin today: ISSUE nodes (type=ISSUE, deterministic id issue::shape-violation::<callId>, name string, file, metadata JSON with severity/category/method/receiverType/callName/line) — NODES, which @materialize cannot create
proposed rule-pack: SHAPE_VIOLATION edges CALL → CLASS/INTERFACE (binary head, mode=exclusive — the type is owned solely by this pack, so fixed violations retract on re-run)
blockers: ISSUE node creation: @materialize writes EDGES from binary heads only (materialize.rs plan_writeback rejects non-binary heads; there is no node write-back path at all) — the entire ISSUE-node output is inexpressible

metadata payload: @materialize attaches only its own provenance stamp (rule_ast_hash + generation, materialize.rs provenance_metadata); there is no way to project body bindings (method name, receiverType name, callName, line) into edge or node metadata

% shape_verifier.dl — in-engine replacement for plugins/shape-verifier.mjs
% (60s-timeout N+1 IPC plugin → one bottom-up program).
%
% Flags dotted CALLs whose receiver's declared type (CLASS/INTERFACE, EXTENDS-closed)
% lacks the called member, as SHAPE_VIOLATION edges CALL → type node.
% MUST run AFTER method_calls.dl: the unresolved-call filter reads CALLS as EDB.
% Unlike method_calls.dl, \+ edge(C,_,"CALLS") is stratifier-clean HERE because this
% program does not materialize CALLS (no storage-level self-dependency).

% A dotted CALL and its method-name suffix ("kb.queryNodes" -> "queryNodes").
call_method(C, MName) :-
    node(C, "CALL"),
    attr(C, "name", FullName),
    method_suffix(FullName, MName).

% Plugin parity: only verify calls the resolver could not resolve.
unresolved_call(C, MName) :-
    call_method(C, MName),
    \+ edge(C, _, "CALLS"),
    \+ edge(C, _, "CALLS_REMOTE").

% Receiver chain (identical to method_calls.dl): direct READS_FROM, or via the
% callee PROPERTY_ACCESS; deref one REFERENCE hop, identity otherwise.
receiver_var(C, V) :- node(C, "CALL"), edge(C, V, "READS_FROM").
receiver_var(C, V) :-
    node(C, "CALL"),
    edge(C, PA, "DERIVES_FROM"),
    node(PA, "PROPERTY_ACCESS"),
    edge(PA, V, "READS_FROM").
receiver_decl(C, D) :- receiver_var(C, V), node(V, "REFERENCE"), edge(V, D, "READS_FROM").
receiver_decl(C, D) :- receiver_var(C, D), \+ node(D, "REFERENCE").

% Types whose shape the plugin indexed (a shape with zero members still counts).
shape_known(T) :- node(T, "CLASS").
shape_known(T) :- node(T, "INTERFACE").

% Member names, EXTENDS-closed (plugin's collectMethods; the fixpoint subsumes its
% visited-set cycle guard). Interfaces additionally contribute HAS_PROPERTY names.
member_name(T, MName) :- edge(T, M, "HAS_METHOD"), attr(M, "name", MName).
member_name(T, MName) :- node(T, "INTERFACE"), edge(T, P, "HAS_PROPERTY"), attr(P, "name", MName).
member_name(T, MName) :- edge(T, P, "EXTENDS"), member_name(P, MName).

% The receiver's declared type, restricted to known shapes (the plugin's
% classMethodIndex.get(...) miss → continue).
receiver_shape(C, T) :- receiver_decl(C, D), edge(D, T, "INSTANCE_OF"), shape_known(T).

% A call is shape-ok if ANY known receiver shape carries the member (replaces the
% plugin's order-dependent first-INSTANCE_OF pick — strictly fewer false positives).
shape_ok(C) :- unresolved_call(C, MName), receiver_shape(C, T), member_name(T, MName).

% The violation: exclusive mode — SHAPE_VIOLATION is owned solely by this pack,
% so a violation fixed in code (or newly resolved) retracts on the next run.
@materialize(edge_type = "SHAPE_VIOLATION", mode = "exclusive")
shape_violation(C, T) :-
    unresolved_call(C, MName),
    receiver_shape(C, T),
    \+ member_name(T, MName),
    \+ shape_ok(C).

spec.purpose: Detects cross-process/cross-language IPC boundaries and writes CALLS_REMOTE edges from the sender's enclosing function to the receiver's entry point. It (1) finds CALL nodes matching a hardcoded table of IPC primitives (spawn/execFile/fork, net.connect, Socket.write, fetch/http.request, RFDBClient/RFDBServerBackend constructors, Rust send_raw/send_command/Command::new), filtered by source language via file extension; (2) extracts a "channel identity" (binary name / socket path / URL) by tracing the call's first argument through PASSES_ARGUMENT → LITERAL or depth-10 READS_FROM/ASSIGNED_FROM dataflow chains, with string cleanup (quote stripping, basename, template-quasi parsing, camelCase service-name extraction) and channelHint fallbacks; (3) matches the channel to a receiver — config.yaml service entry points, the rfdb server's handle_request_with_cancel, http:route nodes by URL-path pattern; (4) writes CALLS_REMOTE edges with {transport, channel} metadata, ISSUE nodes for unresolved bridges, and config-driven bridges from run_batch_plugin/run_streaming_plugin to plugin script MODULEs (creating virtual MODULE nodes when the script is out of analysis scope). It times out because every arg-trace step and containing-function walk is a separate getNode/getOutgoingEdges/getIncomingEdges IPC round-trip.

edge types: CONTAINS, HAS_SCOPE, HAS_BODY/HAS_CONSEQUENT/HAS_ALTERNATE/HAS_CATCH/HAS_FINALLY (descendant walk), PASSES_ARGUMENT (with .index edge attr), READS_FROM, ASSIGNED_FROM, DERIVES_FROM, HAS_ELEMENT (with .index), CALLS, CALLS_REMOTE (dedup read)
node attrs: name, file, line, semanticId, metadata JSON (LITERAL.quasis for template literals; http:route.path)
EXTERNAL (not graph): .grafema/config.yaml — services[].name/path/entryPoint (service index) and plugins[].command/mode (config-driven bridges)

Per-edge custom metadata: plan_writeback emits only fixed provenance metadata (rule_ast_hash, generation); the plugin's {transport, channel, configDriven} edge payload cannot be expressed — transport can be encoded per-rule only by splitting edge types, channel value not at all
Edge-attribute access: selecting arg0 needs PASSES_ARGUMENT.index (and HAS_ELEMENT.index ordering); datalog2 attr() reads node attrs only

String ops beyond suffix-after-dot: cleanStringLiteral (quote stripping), basename(), new URL().pathname, template-quasi extraction from metadata JSON, extractServiceName (camelCase split + boilerplate filter), matchPathPattern ({param} regex) — none expressible; string_contains/starts_with only filter already-clean bound strings
ends_with missing: exact language gating (.ts/.js/.mjs/.rs) and socket-path basename matching approximated by string_contains

Choice/preference semantics: 'first/best candidate' logic everywhere (candidates.find prefer path-like, entry-name priority main>activate>run>start, first CONTAINS parent, depth-limited first hit) — datalog derives ALL matches; priority is expressible via layered stratified negation but changes cardinality vs the plugin

url_path(Url, Path) — Function, Url bound: pathname of an absolute URL, identity for path-only strings. Unblocks the http transport channel

path_pattern_match(Pattern, Path) — Filter, both bound: route patterns with {param} segments match concrete paths ('/api/hex-batch/{batch_id}' vs '/api/hex-batch/123'). Unblocks http receiver matching without exposing regex

NOT proposed as builtins: extractServiceName (camelCase heuristics) and config.yaml access — the heuristic belongs outside the engine; config belongs in the graph as config:service / config:plugin facts ingested by the orchestrator, after which receiver lookup becomes an ordinary join

% semantic_bridge.dl — in-engine core of plugins/semantic-bridge-detector.mjs.
% Materializes CALLS_REMOTE for the IPC bridges decidable from graph structure
% alone: the channelHint paths (rfdb client/server) and self-spawn. The plugin's
% string/config machinery (literal cleaning, basename, URL parsing, YAML services,
% ISSUE nodes, virtual MODULE nodes) is NOT expressible — see migration spec.
%
% mode = "additive": CALLS_REMOTE stays shared with the residual config-driven JS
% half of the plugin; exclusive write-back would tombstone its edges. The plugin's
% "bridge already exists" check (step 4) is exactly the additive dedup at commit —
% an in-program \+ edge(S, R, "CALLS_REMOTE") would be negation on the type this
% program materializes, which the stratifier rejects (same note as method_calls.dl).

% ── Language gates (extension check; string_contains approximates the missing
%    ends_with builtin — adequate for this repo's path shapes; ".tsx" ⊃ ".ts") ──
js_call(C)   :- node(C, "CALL"), attr(C, "file", F), string_contains(F, ".ts").
js_call(C)   :- node(C, "CALL"), attr(C, "file", F), string_contains(F, ".js").
js_call(C)   :- node(C, "CALL"), attr(C, "file", F), string_contains(F, ".mjs").
rust_call(C) :- node(C, "CALL"), attr(C, "file", F), string_contains(F, ".rs").

% ── Sender primitives (the SENDER_PRIMITIVES table, per-name rules; method_suffix
%    covers dotted receivers like child_process.spawn / self.send_raw) ──
subprocess_call(C) :- js_call(C), attr(C, "name", "spawn").
subprocess_call(C) :- js_call(C), attr(C, "name", "execFile").
subprocess_call(C) :- js_call(C), attr(C, "name", "fork").

spec.purpose: Detects Axum `.route("/path", get(handler))` calls in Rust files: scans every CALL node named "route" whose file ends in .rs, validates arg 0 is a LITERAL starting with "/" (the route path) and arg 1 is a CALL named get/post/put/delete/patch/head/options (the HTTP-method wrapper), then CREATES a synthetic `http:route` node (id = "http:route:METHOD:PATH@file", metadata {method, path, framework:"axum"}, exported, line) plus an EXPOSES edge (route CALL → http:route) and a HANDLES edge (http:route → wrapper's first argument = the handler). Runs after analysis, before semantic-bridge-detector. It currently does N+1 IPC: per route-call getOutgoingEdges + getNode per arg + getOutgoingEdges on the wrapper → 60s timeout.
reads: node type CALL (name == 'route' exact-match; wrapper names get/post/put/delete/patch/head/options)
node type LITERAL (attr name = the path string, tested with startsWith('/'))
handler node (any type — whatever the wrapper's argument resolves to, typically FUNCTION)
attr: name, file (endsWith '.rs'), line (only copied onto the created node)
edge type PASSES_ARGUMENT — including its `index` metadata field for arg ordering (args[0]=path, args[1]=wrapper; wrapper's args[0]=handler), which datalog2's edge/3 does NOT expose
writes: http:route NODES (id 'http:route:METHOD:PATH@file', name 'METHOD PATH', file, line, exported:true, metadata {_source, method, path, framework:'axum'}) — BLOCKED: @materialize cannot create nodes
EXPOSES edges: CALL(route) → http:route — transitively blocked (dst is the synthetic node)
HANDLES edges: http:route → handler — transitively blocked (src is the synthetic node)
Expressible re-shape onto EXISTING nodes: HAS_ROUTE_PATH edge CALL(route) → path LITERAL, and ROUTES_TO edge CALL(route) → handler
blockers: Node creation: the plugin's primary output is the synthetic http:route node; @materialize (materialize.rs) projects binary head facts p(A,B) to edges A→B only — both endpoint columns must resolve to EXISTING node ids (resolve to Value::Id), so neither the node nor any edge touching it (EXPOSES, HANDLES) is producible in-engine

% axum_routes.dl — partial in-engine port of plugins/axum-route-detector.mjs
% (the 60s-timeout batch plugin: N+1 IPC per route call -> one bottom-up program).
%
% NOT ported (inexpressible): the synthetic http:route NODE with {method, path,
% framework} metadata, and the EXPOSES/HANDLES edges that touch it — @materialize
% writes EDGES between existing nodes only. This pack materializes the underlying
% binary relations instead:
%   HAS_ROUTE_PATH : route CALL -> path LITERAL   (path readable as the LITERAL's name)
%   ROUTES_TO      : route CALL -> handler        (method readable as the wrapper CALL's name)
% Both edge types are OWNED by this pack (no analyzer writes them), hence
% mode = "exclusive": reanalysis supersedes — stale routes are tombstoned on rerun
% (contrast method_calls.dl, where CALLS is shared with analyzers => additive).
%
% No negation anywhere: the plugin never filters already-processed calls, so the
% method_calls.dl stratifier hazard (negation on the materialized type) does not arise.

% A .route(...) call in a Rust file. method_suffix = suffix after the LAST dot,
% so method_suffix(File, "rs") is the in-engine ".rs" extension test.
route_call(C, File) :-
    node(C, "CALL"),
    attr(C, "name", "route"),
    attr(C, "file", File),
    method_suffix(File, "rs").

% The route-path argument: a LITERAL argument whose value starts with "/".
% (The plugin used PASSES_ARGUMENT index 0; edge indexes are not readable in-engine —
% the literal-shape test stands in for the position test, same validation the plugin
% itself applies before accepting arg 0.)
route_path_arg(C, P) :-
    route_call(C, _),
    edge(C, P, "PASSES_ARGUMENT"),
    node(P, "LITERAL"),
    attr(P, "name", Path),
    starts_with(Path, "/").

@materialize(edge_type = "HAS_ROUTE_PATH", mode = "exclusive")
route_path(C, P) :- route_path_arg(C, P).

% Recognized HTTP-method wrapper calls (axum routing fns are lowercase, so the
% plugin's toLowerCase() is a no-op on real axum code; one clause per method).
is_http_wrapper(W) :- node(W, "CALL"), attr(W, "name", "get").
is_http_wrapper(W) :- node(W, "CALL"), attr(W, "name", "post").
is_http_wrapper(W) :- node(W, "CALL"), attr(W, "name", "put").
is_http_wrapper(W) :- node(W, "CALL"), attr(W, "name", "delete").
is_http_wrapper(W) :- node(W, "CALL"), attr(W, "name", "patch").
is_http_wrapper(W) :- node(W, "CALL"), attr(W, "name", "head").
is_http_wrapper(W) :- node(W, "CALL"), attr(W, "name", "options").

% Route -> handler: the handler is an argument of the route call's HTTP wrapper
% argument (plugin: wrapper's arg 0; real axum wrappers take exactly one argument,
% so "any argument" coincides with index 0 in practice). Guarded on a valid path
% argument — parity with the plugin's `if (!routePath.startsWith('/')) continue`.
@materialize(edge_type = "ROUTES_TO", mode = "exclusive")
route_handler(C, H) :-
    route_path_arg(C, _),
    edge(C, W, "PASSES_ARGUMENT"),
    is_http_wrapper(W),
    edge(W, H, "PASSES_ARGUMENT").

Migration architecture recommendation: two-stage. Stage 1 (this pack) moves the entire O(calls x args) join in-engine — this is what kills the 60s timeout. Stage 2 is a THIN node-shim plugin (or a rewrite of semantic-bridge-detector's input contract): it queries only the materialized ROUTES_TO/HAS_ROUTE_PATH edges (O(#routes), typically tens, not N+1 over the whole CALL set) and mints the http:route nodes + EXPOSES/HANDLES from them; method = wrapper CALL's name (reachable from the route CALL's PASSES_ARGUMENT wrapper), path = the HAS_ROUTE_PATH target LITERAL's name. Alternatively Stage 2 dissolves entirely if/when the @materialize node-creation directive lands. Caveat for the shim: per MEMORY, use direct client.addNodes/addEdges, not BatchHandle (BatchHandle.commit tombstones existing nodes in changed files).

Parity deltas vs the plugin, all documented in the draft: (1) shape-based instead of index-based arg identification (edge `index` metadata unreadable); (2) no 'default GET' route fact when the second arg is not a recognized wrapper (that branch only mattered for node metadata); (3) lowercase-literal method matching instead of toLowerCase (exact for real axum). The plugin has no already-resolved filter, so no negation is needed and the E-STRAT-001 hazard from method_calls.dl does not apply; exclusive mode is correct here because HAS_ROUTE_PATH/ROUTES_TO are pack-owned types.

problems: PARITY MISCHARACTERIZED (blocker bullet + r5 fixture rationale): the plugin extracts a handler from ANY CALL second-argument, not only recognized HTTP wrappers — in plugins/axum-route-detector.mjs:60-72 the handler lookup is inside `if (methodCall ... === 'CALL')` but OUTSIDE the `HTTP_METHODS.has(methodName)` check. `.route("/raw", my_service(state))` makes the plugin emit HANDLES -> state (method defaults to GET). The spec claims that branch 'still creates a route node with no handler' — false whenever the unrecognized call has arguments. The draft's is_http_wrapper gate on route_handler is strictly narrower than the plugin; that may be the RIGHT engineering choice (the plugin's handler-from-any-CALL is sloppy, and without edge `index` the draft would fan out to ALL args of a multi-arg call instead of the plugin's lowest-index one), but it must be documented as a deliberate narrowing, and the r5 fixture comment corrected (r5 only matches plugin behavior because its my_service call is given no PASSES_ARGUMENT args; add an r6 with my_service(state) to pin the documented divergence: plugin emits a handler edge, the pack does not).

EDGE-TYPE COLLISION RISK (question 4): 'ROUTES_TO ... OWNED by this pack (no analyzer writes them)' is unsafe under mode=exclusive. ROUTES_TO is pre-registered product vocabulary: packages/types/src/edges.ts:80 plus the RouteEdge interface at edges.ts:220 (`type: 'ROUTES_TO' | 'HANDLED_BY'` carrying method/path — implying http:route -> handler endpoints, not CALL -> handler), traversed by GUI flow config (packages/gui/src/config/flows.ts:21) and cited in CLI docs (packages/cli/src/commands/context.ts:68). No producer exists today (grep over packages/*/src and plugins/: zero addEdge sites), so nothing is tombstoned NOW, but exclusive write-back deletes every underived stored edge of the type — any future producer adopting the registered type (e.g. an express/library enricher) gets its edges silently tombstoned, and the draft repurposes the type with different endpoint semantics. Fix: rename to a genuinely pack-owned type (HAS_ROUTE_HANDLER — verified collision-free in packages/, plugins/, grafema-orchestrator/) and let the Stage-2 shim mint the product-vocabulary EXPOSES/HANDLES edges.

UNDOCUMENTED PARITY DELTA: the plugin skips route calls with fewer than 2 PASSES_ARGUMENT edges (axum-route-detector.mjs:47 `if (args.length < 2) continue`). A route call whose ONLY argument is a slash-literal derives HAS_ROUTE_PATH in the draft but nothing in the plugin. Inexpressible without an arg-count/aggregation builtin; negligible for real axum (.route always takes 2 args) but must be listed in the parity deltas.
